themes_detail.label: Food Poisoning Cluster
themes_detail.summary: Food poisoning complaints in Bed-Stuy spiked to 4 THIS WEEK, a 540% increase from the 0.6 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.97), suggesting a potential outbreak or food safety violation wave requiring immediate restaurant inspection investigation.
evidence: 4 food poisoning complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 6.97 indicates statistically significant spike
Community Board has standing request to 'Increase health and safety inspections for restaurants and childcare programs' — suggests prior inspectional gaps
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH to identify which restaurants/food vendors are under investigation this week
Interview residents who filed complaints to identify common symptoms, venues, or timeline

themes_detail.label: Non-Emergency Police Complaint Surge
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matters jumped to 20 complaints 2 weeks ago, a 540% increase from the 3.1 weekly average (z-score: 10.99), indicating a significant shift in public safety concerns or neighborhood policing issues requiring clarification.
evidence: 20 non-emergency police complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 10.99 (highest-ranking spike in dataset), indicating extreme statistical significance
Pattern suggests concentrated incident(s) rather than gradual deterioration
reporting_angles: FOIL request or 311 detail query to identify specific types of non-emergency complaints (quality-of-life, harassment, trespassing, etc.)
Canvas beat cops and precinct leadership to understand if spike was incident-driven or reflects changing complaint behavior

themes_detail.label: Vacant/Degraded Lot Problem
themes_detail.summary: Lot condition complaints exploded to 7 complaints 2 weeks ago, a 2700% increase from the 0.2 weekly average (z-score: 10.21), suggesting rapid deterioration of outdoor spaces or emergence of new abandoned/neglected properties.
evidence: 7 lot condition complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 10.21 (second-highest spike), indicating extraordinary statistical anomaly
Convergence with Community Board's repeated budget request for 'new or expanded parks/amenities' — suggests chronic underinvestment in public space
reporting_angles: Geo-map the 7 complaints to identify if they cluster around specific blocks or are scattered across district
Check HPD/DOB records for recent tax foreclosures, ownership changes, or code violations on identified lots

themes_detail.label: Obstruction & Street Infrastructure Decay
themes_detail.summary: Obstruction complaints (14 two weeks ago, +300% from 3.5 avg, z-score: 6.33) and damaged street signs (3 two weeks ago, +500% from 0.5 avg, z-score: 5.0) both spiked simultaneously 2 weeks ago, indicating deteriorating public right-of-way conditions or construction-related disruptions.
evidence: 14 obstruction complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 3.5 weekly average (z-score: 6.33)
3 street sign complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.5 weekly average (z-score: 5.0)
Concurrent spikes suggest shared cause (construction, weather event, or enforcement lapse)
reporting_angles: Cross-reference DOB active permits from last 2-3 weeks to identify ongoing construction projects
Contact DOT to ask if they've issued street obstruction violations or are aware of specific high-impact blockages

themes_detail.label: Unleashed Dog Complaints Rising
themes_detail.summary: Unleashed dog complaints reached 4 two weeks ago, a 433% increase from the 0.8 weekly average (z-score: 3.92), suggesting emerging animal control or public space safety concerns in residential areas.
evidence: 4 unleashed dog complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.8 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.92 indicates statistically significant (though lower-magnitude) spike
Lower z-score and modest complaint volume suggest localized issue rather than district-wide trend
reporting_angles: Check if complaints cluster around specific parks or blocks
Interview park users and residents to understand if this reflects new dog owners, loss of enforcement, or seasonal pattern
